title: Gifts of the Spirit (1 Corinthians 12)
hook: wisdom, knowledge, faith, healing, tongues: one Spirit, many gifts, one body

segments.voice: Yesterday, sanctification: set apart, then slowly grown into love. Your line was perfect in love.

A letter is being read aloud to a church in Corinth, and the room is tense. Paul has heard things. Some there have spectacular gifts and seem to know it. Others feel they bring nothing. So Paul writes a strange, mixed list: a word of wisdom, a word of knowledge, faith, healing, miracles, prophecy, telling spirits apart, tongues, and the interpreting of tongues. Some sound quiet and some sound loud. And like a drumbeat he repeats one phrase: by the same Spirit. To one this, by the same Spirit. To another that. In this list he isn't ranking anyone. He's tying the whole room together.

Charism is the church's word for a gift of the Spirit: given not as a prize, but for someone else's good. Day two hundred ninety-five met the Pentecostal side of these gifts; today, Paul's chapter itself. It opens, in the King James: "Now there are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit." And why they're given: "the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal." For the common good. A gift that only makes its owner look impressive has missed the point. Then Paul reaches for a body. A foot might say, I'm not a hand, so I'm not part of this. An ear might say, I'm not an eye. If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? Then the line that turns the room around: "the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee." The parts that "seem to be more feeble, are necessary." Not tolerated. Necessary. Christians read this chapter differently. Pentecostal and charismatic churches give great weight to the gifts that show, like healing, prophecy and tongues, and expect them in worship today. Catholic teaching uses charism broadly, for gifts as quiet as teaching or care for the sick, and speaks of whole religious orders having their own charism. Other churches stress gifts like leading, giving and encouraging, which Paul names in Romans. Underneath sits Paul's picture: many gifts, one Spirit, one body. And notice what comes right after this chapter. It's the one about love.
screen: `A GIFT FOR SOMEONE ELSE'S GOOD.` · `DIVERSITIES OF GIFTS, THE SAME SPIRIT.` · `THE EYE CAN'T SAY: NO NEED OF THEE.` · `THE FEEBLE PARTS ARE NECESSARY.` · then, large: `MANY GIFTS, ONE BODY.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person, at church, at work or at home, and skip their obvious talents; look for the quiet gift, like noticing who's left out, or calming a room. Give that gift a name in a few plain words, and sit with the thought that the people around them need it. If you pray, give thanks for that person by name; if you don't, just hold their gift in mind.
Charism. A gift of the Spirit, given for the good of others, one of many in one body.
Your line: many gifts, one spirit. The feeble parts are necessary. I'll be here tomorrow.

howItsDone: Christians read 1 Corinthians 12 as teaching that each member of the church has gifts for the good of all; Pentecostal and charismatic churches expect gifts like healing, prophecy and tongues in worship, and Catholic teaching speaks of many kinds of charisms, including those of religious orders.

fork.setup: you're Paul. some in Corinth flaunt their gifts; others feel they bring nothing. how do you answer?
options: tell the gifted ones to stop using their gifts.
tell the quiet ones their gifts don't count.
say every gift comes from one Spirit, for one body.
fork.reveal: he answers with a body: the eye can't say to the hand "I have no need of thee," and the feeble-seeming parts are necessary.

notes: Hook's list of gifts paraphrases 1 Corinthians 12:8–10; the refrain 'by the same Spirit' is in 12:8–9, with 'the selfsame Spirit' in 12:11; the voice says 'again and again', and the hook's 'To one this, by the same Spirit' is a paraphrase of that pattern.
The tense setting in Corinth (some proud of gifts, others feeling they bring nothing) is inferred from 1 Corinthians 12:14–26 and chapters 13–14; confirm framing.
Summaries of Pentecostal/charismatic, Catholic (charisms broadly, charisms of religious orders) and other churches' emphases: confirm they are fair and unranked.
Original and trapdoor: χάρισμα and its link to χάρις are in games only; confirm.
Do not anticipate day 1095 (tongues) beyond naming tongues in the list.
